text: Before verification: the consent prompt shows 'Unverified' instead of a publisher name.
quote: If the app isn't publisher verified, "Unverified" is displayed instead of a publisher name.

text: Before verification: with risk-based step-up consent on, users in other tenants can't consent to multitenant apps registered after 8 Nov 2020 that ask for more than sign-in and profile.
quote: The policy applies to apps that were registered after November 8, 2020, which use OAuth 2.0 to request permissions that extend beyond the basic sign-in and read user profile
note: Page says users can't consent to "most" newly registered unverified multitenant apps; the claim restates the policy scope.

text: Register the app in Microsoft Entra ID as at least an Application Developer.
quote: Sign in to the Microsoft Entra admin center as at least an Application Developer.

text: For other organizations, set supported account types to multiple Entra ID tenants, with or without personal Microsoft accounts.
quote: Multiple Entra ID tenants For multitenant apps when you want users in any Microsoft Entra tenant to be able to use your application.
note: Also lists "Any Entra ID Tenant + Personal Microsoft accounts".

text: Publisher verification needs a verified Microsoft AI Cloud Partner Program (formerly MPN) partner global account ID.
quote: The developer must have a Partner One ID for a valid Microsoft AI Cloud Partner Program account that has completed the verification process. The CPP account must be the partner global account (PGA)

text: The app must be registered with a work or school account, not a personal Microsoft account, to be publisher verified.
quote: Apps that are registered by using a Microsoft account can't be publisher verified.

text: The publisher domain can't be *.onmicrosoft.com and must match the Partner Center email domain or a DNS-verified custom domain.
quote: (NOTE__: the app's publisher domain can't be *.onmicrosoft.com to be publisher verified)
note: Page: CPP verification email domain must match the publisher domain or a DNS-verified custom domain on the tenant.

text: The person verifying needs Application Administrator or Cloud Application Administrator in Entra, and Microsoft AI Cloud Partner Program Admin or Accounts Admin in Partner Center, and must sign in with MFA.
quote: The user in Partner Center must have the following roles: Microsoft AI Cloud Partner Program Admin or Accounts Admin.
note: Entra roles Application Administrator or Cloud Application Administrator and MFA sign-in also stated.

text: Delegated ChannelMessage.Read.All and TeamMember.Read.All require admin consent.
quote: Allows an app to read a channel's messages in Microsoft Teams, on behalf of the signed-in user.
note: Graph table: ChannelMessage.Read.All and TeamMember.Read.All both show AdminConsentRequired = Yes in the Delegated column.

text: Delegated Chat.Read, Chat.ReadWrite, ChatMessage.Send, ChannelMessage.Send and Team.ReadBasic.All don't need admin consent.
quote: Allows an app to send channel messages in Microsoft Teams, on behalf of the signed-in user.
note: Graph table: Chat.Read, Chat.ReadWrite, ChatMessage.Send, ChannelMessage.Send and Team.ReadBasic.All all show AdminConsentRequired = No in the Delegated column.

text: For apps that need admin consent, add an admin sign-up link that sends prompt=consent so one admin approves for the whole tenant.
quote: If your application uses permissions that require admin consent, consider adding a button or link where the admin can initiate the action.
note: Same paragraph: the request includes prompt=consent, and afterwards no other users in the tenant are prompted for consent.

text: Application (app-only) permissions always need tenant admin consent.
quote: App-only permissions always require a tenant administrator’s consent.

text: Tenant admins can turn off user consent, which makes admin consent mandatory for every app in that tenant.
quote: If this capability is disabled, admin consent is always required for the application to be used in the tenant.
note: Preceding sentence: a tenant administrator can disable the ability for regular users to consent to applications.

text: Microsoft recommends tenants allow user consent only for apps from verified publishers.
quote: we recommend that you allow user consent only for applications that have been published by a verified publisher.

text: If an admin consents without prompt=consent, the consent only covers the admin's own account.
quote: when the admin successfully consents to the application it applies only for their user account.
note: Condition in same sentence: app requires admin consent and admin signs in without prompt=consent.

text: Client secrets last 24 months at most, and Microsoft recommends under 12 months.
quote: Client secret lifetime is limited to two years (24 months) or less.
note: Next line: "Microsoft recommends that you set an expiration value of less than 12 months."

text: Refresh tokens last 90 days by default, or 24 hours for single-page app redirect URIs.
quote: 24 hours for single-page applications. 24 hours for apps that use email one-time passcode authentication flow. 90 days for all other scenarios.
note: Page also lists 24 hours for email one-time passcode flows.

text: Multitenant apps must call the /common or /organizations endpoint, not a tenant-specific one.
quote: requests are sent to a common endpoint (https://login.microsoftonline.com/common) that serves across all Microsoft Entra tenants
fix: Multitenant apps send sign-in requests to /common (or /organizations if they don't support personal accounts), but later token calls for an already signed-in user should go to that user's tenant endpoint.
note: Page explicitly says subsequent calls for a signed-in user should use the tenant's endpoint, so "not a tenant-specific one" is overstated.

text: $0: Microsoft doesn't charge for publisher verification and no license is needed
quote: Microsoft doesn't charge developers for publisher verification. No license is required to become a verified publisher.

text: Before approval: a local OAuth client's tokens only access the single Zendesk instance that created it.
quote: An OAuth token gives access to a single Zendesk instance (the one with the OAuth client used to create the token).

text: Third-party apps may not use a customer's API token or the customer's own OAuth client, listed or not.
quote: (whether it’s listed on the Zendesk Marketplace or not) to use a customer’s API credentials (API token or a customer’s own OAuth client) to authenticate API calls.

text: Apps distributed to multiple Zendesk customers must use global OAuth tokens.
quote: If you distribute a public app or an integration app to multiple Zendesk customers, you must use global OAuth tokens to authenticate requests.

text: Requests must come from a d3v- sponsored account; non-d3v- submissions aren't accepted.
quote: Ensure the subdomain includes the prefix d3v-. Submissions from non-d3v- accounts aren't accepted.

text: Sponsored d3v- accounts are reserved for developers building Zendesk Marketplace apps.
quote: A sponsored test account is reserved for developers creating applications for the Zendesk Marketplace.

text: The local client's unique identifier must start with zdg- and every field must be filled in.
quote: Make sure all fields are completed for the local client. Even if a field is labeled optional, it is required for global clients.
note: Same list: "Ensure your Unique Identifier is prefixed with the string \"zdg-\"."

text: Unlisted integrations must still create a Marketplace profile, register the organization and submit for review.
quote: If you haven’t listed your integration on the Zendesk Marketplace, you need to create your Zendesk Marketplace profile, register your organization and submit your app for review and approval.

text: Global OAuth clients must support the refresh token flow from January 31, 2026.
quote: Supporting the refresh token flow will be required for all global OAuth clients starting January 31, 2026.

text: Save the client secret and identifier first; you lose the client admin page after conversion to global.
quote: Make sure you note down the secret and the identifier before making your request. You will lose access to the client administration page after the local client is converted to a global client.

text: Zendesk may cap allowed scopes; requesting others returns 400 invalid_scope.
quote: If your app requests a scope that is not included in the client's allowed scopes, the authorization request fails with a 400 Bad Request response and an invalid_scope error

text: Scope changes after approval go through Zendesk Support, since only Marketplace Operations can edit global clients.
quote: Because global clients can only be edited by the Zendesk Marketplace operations team, you'll need to contact Zendesk Support to request a change to your client's allowed scopes.

text: New global clients get 30-minute access tokens and 30-day refresh tokens by default.
quote: we are enforcing the default TTL (time to live) for access and refresh tokens for (1) all newly created global OAuth clients
note: TTL table: access token default 30 minutes (min 5 min, max 48 h); refresh token default 30 days (min 7, max 90 days).

text: A sponsored account is suspended if used to provide real customer support.
quote: Note: Zendesk will suspend any sponsored Support account used to provide actual support.

text: Integration apps must send custom headers identifying the integration, organization ID and Marketplace app ID.
quote: each API call must include custom headers that specify the name of the integration, the organization ID, and the Marketplace app ID.

text: Global OAuth client request through the Zendesk Marketplace portal | wait: not stated
quote: Sign in to the Zendesk Marketplace portal. Select Global OAuth from the menu on the left side, and then click the Request new OAuth button.
note: No review duration is stated on the page.

text: No fee is mentioned for the global OAuth request
note: Page contains no mention of any fee, cost or charge.

text: Private apps can only be used inside the account that built them.
quote: Private apps are those developed for use inside the same monday account. Users outside of the account can't access or use the app

text: Shared apps without monday approval show a banner saying monday hasn't vetted them.
quote: applications without monday approval will show a banner to indicate that the monday.com team hasn't vetted them

text: You can restrict a shared app to specific monday accounts.
quote: You can select Share with specific monday accounts and list their account URLs if you want to restrict access to specific accounts.

text: Create the app in the Developer Center; viewers cannot access it.
quote: Viewers can't access the Developer Center

text: Accept the developer terms on the Share tab to get a shareable install link.
quote: Accept the developer terms and click Share App.
note: Steps: navigate to the Share tab, accept terms, copy the shareable URL.

text: Requested scopes must match the scopes configured on the app.
quote: All requested scopes must match the list you configured in your app.

text: Redirect URI must match one of the redirect URLs added to the app.
quote: URL to redirect back on approval/denial. Must match one of the redirect URLs added to your app.

text: Marketplace apps are reviewed on product, engineering, security, privacy, support, docs and legal.
quote: assessing the product, engineering, security, privacy, content, assets, support, documentation, and legal aspects.
fix: Marketplace apps are reviewed on product, engineering, security, privacy, content, assets, support, documentation and legal.
note: Claim omits content and assets from the review areas.

text: If the app is not installed in the workspace, users see 'App is not installed'.
quote: If the app is not installed, Monday can stop the connection flow with an "App is not installed" message.

text: A workspace admin installs the app once; then users can connect.
quote: A Monday workspace admin only needs to install the app once per workspace. After the admin approves the installation, users in that workspace can connect their Monday accounts normally.
note: Text is in the FAQ accordion (embedded page data).

text: Legacy OAuth tokens do not expire and there are no refresh tokens.
quote: Tokens do not expire and are valid until the user uninstalls your app. Our OAuth flow does not support refresh tokens.
note: Page labels this the current (legacy) flow.

text: A newer OAuth 2.1 flow adds expiring access tokens and refresh tokens.
quote: monday.com now supports an improved OAuth 2.1 flow with expiring access tokens, refresh tokens, and token revocation.

text: The authorization code is valid for only 10 minutes.
quote: The authorization code is only valid for 10 minutes

text: New apps built mainly with no-code tools or AI 'vibe code' are not eligible for the marketplace.
quote: New apps built primarily using no-code platforms or AI-generated “vibe code” are not eligible for marketplace approval.

text: Rate limit is per user: 50 requests/min on Free plans, 500/min on paid plans.
quote: Rate limits are enforced per user.
note: Table: Paid Plans 500 requests per user per minute; Free Plan 50 requests per user per minute.

text: Only 8 OAuth tokens per user can be requested within one minute.
quote: Only 8 OAuth tokens per user can be requested within a span of 1 minute.

text: Webhook subscriptions need the user on a paid Standard, Teams or Enterprise plan.
quote: the Calendly user account for which the webhook subscription is being made will need a paid subscription on the Standard, Teams, or Enterprise plan.

text: Sign up for a developer account with GitHub or Google; it is separate from your Calendly user account.
quote: Note: This is not your Calendly user account and is not associated with your Calendly user account.
note: Same step: sign up for a developer account using your Github or Google account.

text: Production apps must use an HTTPS redirect URI; Sandbox allows http localhost.
quote: For the Sandbox environment, we allow HTTP with localhost domain. Example: http://localhost:1234
note: Next line: "For the Production environment, this must be HTTPS".

text: Calendly recommends a Sandbox app for development and a second app for Production.
quote: We recommend starting with Sandbox for development and creating a second application for Production when ready to go live with customer data.

text: The client secret and webhook signing key are shown only once at creation.
quote: these values are only displayed when the OAuth application is created
note: Refers to Client Secret and Webhook signing key.

text: Access tokens expire after 2 hours.
quote: Access Tokens expire after 2 hours.

text: Refresh tokens are single-use and rotate on every refresh.
quote: each refresh token can only be used once — when you use it to refresh, that refresh token becomes invalid and you’ll get a new refresh token in the response.
note: Page frames this as a rollout ("Going forward"), already active for new apps, with a grace period for older apps.

text: Tokens are revoked if the user changes login email, password or login method.
quote: Both OAuth and personal access tokens will be revoked if:
note: Listed conditions: login email changed, password changed, login method changed.

text: Users cannot approve individual scopes; the app's configured scopes are requested.
quote: Calendly does not let end users selectively approve individual scopes during the OAuth connection flow. The scopes configured in your Calendly OAuth app are the scopes that will be requested
note: Text is in the FAQ accordion (embedded page data).

text: A few endpoints require the Enterprise plan.
quote: with the exception of a few endpoints that are specific to our Enterprise plan

text: If an enterprise turns on Disable unpublished apps by default, its admin must enable your OAuth 2.0 app first.
quote: Enable in **Integrations** > **Platform Apps Manager** > **User Authentication Apps** > Select Platform App > Use **More** menu to enable the app.
note: OAuth 2.0 row of the "Disable unpublished apps by default" table, Enabled column; Disabled column says Ready for use.

text: Redirect URIs must be HTTPS, or HTTP only for localhost or loopback addresses.
quote: These must be valid URIs that are HTTPS, or a less secure HTTP for localhost or loopback address.

text: Box Integrations listing accepts only OAuth 2.0 apps that are finished and production-ready.
quote: The platform app leverages OAuth 2.0 authentication, as Integrations do not support any other authentication methods.
note: Prior bullet: "The platform app is in a finished state and ready for production usage."

text: You cannot change the authentication method after creating the app.
quote: Once you make a selection, you will not be able to change to a different authentication method without creating a new application.

text: Refresh tokens are single-use and expire after 60 days, after which users must re-authorize.
quote: A Refresh Token is valid for 60 days and can be used to obtain a new Access Token and Refresh Token only once.
note: Also: if not refreshed within 60 days, the user will need to be re-authorized.

text: Admins enable an OAuth 2.0 app by entering its client ID under Platform > Platform Apps.
quote: In the top-right corner of the window, click Add + then enter the user authentication application client ID.
note: Path: Admin Console > Platform > Platform Apps tab > User Authentication Apps; then select a state and Apply. An emailed-request route also exists.

text: Box disables all unpublished platform apps when that enterprise setting is on.
quote: When you select Disable unpublished platform apps by default, Box disables all unpublished platform apps by default.
fix: With Disable unpublished platform apps by default on, Box disables unpublished platform apps whose status an admin never manually changed; admins can re-enable them in Platform Apps.
note: Same page says the setting "only affects apps whose status has not been manually changed by an admin", so "all" is overstated.

text: Redirect URIs are checked by exact match.
quote: This will be an exact match check, meaning the URIs must be exactly the same.
note: Localhost and loopback URIs may redirect to any port.
